titre: Recognition for Flemish hops to encourage breweries to use local
extrait: Hops and hop shoots from Asse and the surrounding area have now been recognised as a Flemish regional product. The Flemish Centre for Agricultural and Fisheries Marketing (VLAM) made the award celebrating the local hop growing industry. Hops are used for many purposes but above all to make beer, and their cultivation in the region dates back to the 15th century.

titre: Cactus Club in Oudergem closes after 40 years: “Partying in nightclubs is out of fashion”
extrait: The Cactus Club in Oudergem (Brussels) is closing for good on 2 January. After 40 years of partying, the nightclub wants to call it a day whilst it’s still at the top of its game. “The years ahead would look catastrophic,” says owner Philippe Harlet.

titre: Du changement à venir sur MyPension : plus de 4,5 millions d’affiliés concernés
extrait: L’instauration de ce relevé des droits à la retraite uniforme remplacera les anciennes fiches de pension, envoyée par les organismes financiers. Jusqu’ici, chaque organisme présentait sa fiche à sa manière, en l’envoyant une fois par an.

titre: Vase by Picasso’s daughter turns up at Flemish charity shop
extrait: A vase by Picasso’s daughter, Paloma Picasso, has been discovered at the charity shop in Bornem (Antwerp Province). The vintage vase dates from the 1990s and was used at the time to promote Paloma’s perfume. It is not clear how much it is worth. The vase will be auctioned via the charity shop’s website.

titre: Fleming wins Emmy for AI technology: ‘Making Tom Hanks 20 years old again’
extrait: The company BRAHMA AI, founded by Flemish entrepreneur Jo Plaete, has won a Technology & Engineering Emmy Award for AI-based visual effects. The technology allows actors in films to be made to look decades younger or to speak a different language, whilst their voice and facial expressions remain the same. “This means a Flemish film can also conquer the American market.”

titre: First swans return to Bruges canal
extrait: The first swans are back in Bruges. The swans at 't Stil Ende waterway had to be moved away during the summer because blue-green algae caused the water quality to deteriorate, but they have now returned. Swans from other Bruges’ canals will remain in the enclosure for the time being. The city is continuing to monitor the water quality of its waterways.

titre: «Eux aussi, on leur disait de retourner étudier»: pourquoi la révolte des lycéens français rappelle Mai 68

Entre colère générationnelle, récupération politique et tensions avec la police, jusqu’où peut aller la comparaison avec le mouvement historique de 1968?
